name: BorgWarehouse
description: BorgWarehouse is a fast, modern web interface for running a BorgBackup server. It turns your Unraid server into a central destination for Borg backups from your other machines: create and manage repositories, assign SSH keys, set quotas, monitor backup status and storage use, and get alerts by email or Apprise when a backup is late. Clients back up over SSH using borg, Vorta or borgmatic. Before installing: generate two secrets for BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and CRONJOB_KEY (for example with "openssl rand -base64 32" in the Unraid terminal), and set SSH_SERVER_PORT to the same value as the SSH host port. Unraid's own SSH already uses port 22, so the default here is 2222. Status and storage checks run on a schedule outside the container. Install the User Scripts plugin and add the script from the support page to keep the dashboard up to date. OIDC single sign-on (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel and others), SMTP and the LAN settings are under Show more settings.

paths.name: Repositories
paths.description: Where the Borg repositories are stored. Backups can be large, so use a share on the array (or a pool sized for it) rather than appdata.

paths.name: SSH authorized keys
paths.description: Client public keys managed by BorgWarehouse (authorized_keys).

paths.name: SSH host keys
paths.description: The server's SSH host keys, generated on first start. Keep this so clients don't see a host key warning after an update.

ports.name: Web UI port
ports.description: Port for the BorgWarehouse web interface.

ports.name: SSH port
ports.description: Port Borg clients connect to over SSH. Unraid's own SSH uses 22, so pick another port. SSH_SERVER_PORT below must match this value.

variables.name: FQDN
variables.description: Hostname or IP address that Borg clients use to reach this server. It appears in the backup commands BorgWarehouse shows you, e.g. tower.local or backup.example.com.

variables.name: SSH_SERVER_PORT
variables.description: Must match the SSH host port above. It appears in the backup commands BorgWarehouse shows you.

variables.name: BETTER_AUTH_URL
variables.description: The main URL you open BorgWarehouse at, including http:// or https:// and any port, e.g. https://borg.example.com or http://192.168.1.10:3000. Logins from any other address are refused (Invalid origin in the log), so add the others to BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS under Show more settings.

variables.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
variables.description: Secret used to sign login sessions. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32. If empty, a new one is made at every restart and everyone is logged out.

variables.name: CRONJOB_KEY
variables.description: Key for the scheduled status and storage checks. Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32. The User Scripts script reads it from the container, so you don't need to copy it anywhere.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID the app runs as. 99 is Unraid's nobody user. Must not be 0.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 is Unraid's users group. Must not be 0.

variables.name: OIDC_ISSUER_URL
variables.description: OIDC issuer URL (Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, ...), without /.well-known/openid-configuration. Set the redirect URI at your provider to BETTER_AUTH_URL/api/auth/callback/oidc. Users must already exist in BorgWarehouse with the same email; SSO doesn't create accounts.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.description: OIDC client ID.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.description: OIDC client secret.

variables.name: OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME
variables.description: Label on the SSO login button. Defaults to SSO.

variables.name: DISABLE_PASSWORD_LOGIN
variables.description: Allow SSO login only. Only takes effect when an SSO provider is configured.

variables.name: SETUP_SECRET
variables.description: Passphrase required to complete the first-run setup wizard. Recommended if the web UI is reachable from the internet before you've created the admin account.

variables.name: BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS
variables.description: Other URLs you open BorgWarehouse at besides BETTER_AUTH_URL, comma separated, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:3000 when BETTER_AUTH_URL is your reverse proxy domain. Without this, logins from those addresses fail with Invalid origin.

variables.name: SESSION_EXPIRY_SECONDS
variables.description: Login session lifetime in seconds. Defaults to 3600 (1 hour).

variables.name: FQDN_LAN
variables.description: Optional local hostname or IP. BorgWarehouse then also shows backup commands for clients on your LAN.

variables.name: SSH_SERVER_PORT_LAN
variables.description: SSH port for the LAN commands, if different.

variables.name: HIDE_SSH_PORT
variables.description: Leave the port out of the commands BorgWarehouse shows (e.g. when clients set it in ~/.ssh/config).

variables.name: MAIL_SMTP_HOST
variables.description: SMTP server for email alerts.

variables.name: MAIL_SMTP_PORT
variables.description: SMTP port. Defaults to 587.

variables.name: MAIL_SMTP_LOGIN
variables.description: SMTP username.

variables.name: MAIL_SMTP_PWD
variables.description: SMTP password.

variables.name: MAIL_SMTP_FROM
variables.description: From address for alert emails.

variables.name: MAIL_REJECT_SELFSIGNED_TLS
variables.description: Set to false to accept a self-signed certificate on the SMTP server.

variables.name: DISABLE_INTEGRATIONS
variables.description: Turn off API tokens (integrations).

variables.name: DISABLE_DELETE_REPO
variables.description: Prevent anyone from deleting a repository.

variables.name: DISABLE_COMPACT_REPO
variables.description: Prevent anyone from compacting a repository.

variables.name: STORAGE_TARGETS
variables.description: Extra storage locations selectable per repository, comma separated, optionally path|name (e.g. /mnt/offsite|Offsite disk). Each path must also be added as a Path mapping to this container.

variables.name: NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED
variables.description: 1 turns off Next.js anonymous telemetry.
